title: Side D, lately
description: The single file a nightly job writes for the Lately section. Every panel is optional; the page shows 'not connected yet' for any panel it cannot draw. Times are ISO 8601 with an offset and are displayed in Pacific time.

schema_version.description: Version 1. Additive changes keep version 1, so older files still validate. 2026-10-13: rankings lists hold up to ten titles (were five); main_lifts[].best gains optional best_set (which may carry source: manual). 2026-10-13, later: optional top-level analysis (statistics computed from the archive), merged from the pipeline's analysis.schema.json; the lately/ pages draw it. 2026-10-13, re-merge: fantasy.teams[] requires waiver_adds (a statistic), so an analysis block without it no longer validates; lineup_efficiency's values gain waiver_hits_left_on_bench. 2026-10-13, re-merge: no structural change; waiver_adds.values gains all (every add, with best and worst flags) inside the statistic's open values object. 2026-10-17: analysis gains fantasy.quadrant and fantasy.manager_score, teams[].acquisition_split and teams[].draft, watching.s_tier, tier_model, taste_drift, community_gap_by_genre and pace_vs_tier, lifting.strength_index, retention, volume_lag and consistency, listening.entropy, nostalgia, enduring and retention_new_artists, eating.landing and rerank_drift, cross.time_budget and meta.sources_included, all optional; eating.top_ten_churn is removed. 2026-10-18: watching gains by_director, by_studio, by_lead, blockbuster, sequels, language, critics_vs_audience and crowd_agreement; listening's entropy and nostalgia may carry values.weeks and retention_new_artists values.available_from; lifting gains best_held_lift; meta gains attributions. All optional. 2026-10-18, later: tier scores are S = 5 to D = 1 throughout; crowd_agreement's disagreements are {above, below}. 2026-10-18, profiles: watching.taste_profile; listening.artist_survival, artist_survival_all (the pre-sync cohort included), album_listening and discovery_direction. All optional. 2026-10-18, corrections: album_listening rows carry each album's Gini; discovery_direction is by year; hr_b is per five years of release gap. 2026-10-18, splits: main_lifts[] gain optional split and tracked; strength_index.values.splits (chest_back, shoulders_arms, legs) beside the overall index; no hand-entered best is published. 2026-10-18, sessions: strength_index.values.tracked [{name, exercise, sessions, split}] carries the rule's session count; main_lifts[].sessions counts the sessions behind the trend. 2026-10-18, policy: every statistic may carry small_sample (ok, n below min_n, drawn with a tag) and, while not enough data yet, values.first_unit (what the first unit of data is); available_from is removed. eating.safe_bet (optional) and eating.landing's current-ranking version (median_percentile, recent, months). 2026-10-18, zero units: the five fixed-shape values objects (quadrant, manager-score components and composite, acquisition_split, draft) are anyOf the full shape or {first_unit}, so a statistic at zero units validates; the small-sample tag reads "small sample, threshold 30".

sample.description: True for placeholder data. The page also treats data/lately.sample.json as sample regardless of this flag.

sources.description: One entry per feed, keyed by a short id. Chips are shown in key order.

status.description: ok: the last run succeeded. error: the last run failed. stale: no run within the expected schedule. pending: not connected yet (e.g. awaiting API approval). disabled: switched off.

message.description: Short public text shown instead of the status word when not ok, e.g. 'awaiting approval'. Never put error details or secrets here.

updated_at.description: When the job last attempted this source.

last_ok_at.description: When this source last succeeded. Null means it never has. When status is not ok, the panel data is from this time.

week.description: The upcoming or current week. Results cover weeks 1 to week - 1.

sources.description: Source ids contributing to this panel, in display order.

wins_above_expected.description: Actual wins minus all-play expected wins, summed over teams.

favoured.description: Teams favoured this week by projected points.

teams.description: Colin's own teams only. Never include other managers' names or team names.

luck.description: Wins versus expected for this team.

win_probability.description: Chance to win the current week, or null when it can't be estimated. When null the page shows win_probability_note, or 'not available this week' if there is no note.

win_probability_note.description: Optional short public text shown in place of the win-chance bar when win_probability is null (e.g. 'too few weeks'). Ignored when win_probability is a number.

points_above_replacement.description: Points above a replacement starter per game played. Can be negative.

weeks.description: Hours per week by type, oldest week first; the last entry is this week. The page's total is the sum of these, so there is no separate total field.

url.description: The title's Simkl page (required by Simkl's attribution terms).

status.description: 'finished': marked complete in bulk on Simkl, so there is no watch date or season. Finished items always come after watched ones.

currently_watching.description: Shows and anime with status 'watching', most recent activity first, with the season and episode reached.

rankings.description: My top ten of each ranking, best first. The page shows the first five, with a toggle for the rest. Every title links to its Simkl page.

plays_this_month.description: Deprecated and ignored. The page shows the sum of plays_by_hour, so the total and the hour chart cover the same last 30 days.

top_artists.description: Top artists over the last 30 days, most played first.

plays_by_hour.description: Plays in the last 30 days by local hour of day, 0:00 first. Their sum is shown as 'Plays, last 30 days'.

recent.description: The ten restaurants most recently ranked on Beli, newest first. No dates or relative times are published; the order is the only signal.

score.description: Beli score, shown with two decimals.

cuisines.description: Places ranked per cuisine. The page draws at most six named cuisines as bars, scaled to the largest named one. Anything beyond six, and any entry named 'Other', becomes a text line under the chart: 'plus N across K other cuisines' when the individual cuisines are listed, or 'Other: N' when the file only gives a lumped 'Other' count.

unit.description: Unit for every weight and volume in this section.

data_through.description: Date (Pacific) of the newest workout included. Show as 'data through …'.

first_workout.description: Date of the first workout in the history.

machine.description: True for machine and cable variants, so the site can label them.

sessions.description: Sessions with a working set of 1 to 10 reps of this lift, the sessions the trend is drawn from. Below three, the page shows 'n sessions so far' in place of the trend chart. Beside each tracked lift the page shows the rule's own count (strength_index.values.tracked[].sessions) when the file has it.

current.description: Estimated one-rep max from the most recent session (Epley, best working set of 1-10 reps), with that set.

source.description: Optional. Present only when the set was entered by hand rather than coming from Hevy; the page tags it 'logged by hand'.

best_set.description: Optional. The set behind the best, in pounds whatever `unit` says. Shown under the best as 'best set 185 × 4 · 26 Sep'.

best.description: Highest estimated one-rep max in the history.

history.description: Estimated one-rep max per session, oldest first, for a sparkline.

split.description: The split the lift belongs to; the lifting page groups the tracked lifts by it.

tracked.description: True when the lift meets the tracking rule (at least 12 sessions in the last 26 weeks); the pages show tracked lifts.

main_lifts.description: One entry per main lift (one exercise per movement pattern), in display order.

weeks.description: The last 12 weeks, oldest first; weeks start on Monday (Pacific). The last one is the current, unfinished week. volume = weight × reps over working sets.

streak_weeks.description: Consecutive weeks with at least streak_min_sessions workouts, counting back from this week; an unfinished week doesn't break it.

streak_min_sessions.description: Workouts a week needs to count towards the streak.

recent_prs.description: Personal records from the last 30 days, newest first, one per exercise and kind (Hevy's own PR markers). value is in `unit` when measure is the unit, else reps, seconds or metres.

muscle_sets.description: Working sets per primary muscle group (Hevy's labels, e.g. upper_back) for the last 4 weeks; sets[i] belongs to weeks[i]. Cardio left out. groups sorted by total, largest first.

body_weight.description: Body weight measurements from Hevy, full precision to 0.1, oldest first in history.

lifting.description: Strength training from Hevy, collected on my Mac nightly. All weights are in `unit`. The source chip's last_ok_at says when it last updated; data_through is the newest workout's date.

analysis_stat.description: One statistic. With a status other than "ok" there is no value, values or interval: nothing is published but the reason. With small_sample true (status ok, n below min_n) the figures are published and tagged as a small sample.

small_sample.description: True when the statistic is published on fewer than min_n units (status ok, n below min_n): the pages draw its chart and numbers as usual and tag the n line "small sample, threshold 10" (min_n). Absent or false otherwise.

value.description: The headline number, when there is one.

values.description: The statistic's figures; each one's shape is in analysis.sample.json. While status is "not enough data yet", values.first_unit (a string) names the first unit of data the statistic needs, as a phrase ("one album with 10 plays in its first week"); the pages show one line, "nothing to show yet: needs <first_unit>", and nothing else: no count of units needed and no date. (available_from is removed.)

interval.description: 95% interval for value, where one is defined.

n.description: Sample size, in the unit min_n counts (weeks, plays, sessions, places...).

how.description: One plain sentence: how it is computed.

missing.description: Unless ok: the archive field or setting that is lacking.

sources_included.description: The source names present in this file (sleeper, espn, yahoo, simkl, lastfm, beli, hevy); the site renders an absent source cleanly.

attributions.description: Credits the pages must print where these statistics render: text verbatim, as a link when url is given.

analysis.description: Statistics computed from the archive: one block per feed plus cross and grading. Opponents are never named; Beli dates never appear.

platforms.description: Per platform (sleeper, espn), across my teams there.

quadrant.description: Strength against luck for every team in my leagues: x = all-play win share, y = wins above expected. values.mine are my teams with their week-by-week trail; values.others are the other teams, anonymous.

draft.description: Points per week my drafted starters score against the round baseline (value), with rank, of and percentile in values.

lineup.description: Points per week my lineup choices gain or lose against the optimal lineup (value), with rank, of and percentile.

moves.description: Points per week from adds, drops and trades against a no-move baseline (value), with rank, of and percentile.

strength.description: Points per week my roster scores against the league average (value), with rank, of and percentile.

components.description: Each component's value is points per week against its baseline.

composite.description: The four components combined: value and values.percentile are the share of managers I beat (0 to 1), with its interval.

manager_score.description: How good a manager I am, apart from luck: four components and a composite, pooled across my leagues.

name.description: Display name by platform and format; never a team name.

acquisition_split.description: Points to date by how each player arrived (draft, waiver, trade, other), mine against the league median.

draft.description: Every pick of mine against the median for its round (value: the residuals summed).

entropy.description: Shannon entropy of plays across artists, by month with at least 50 plays: values.months [{month, plays, artists, entropy_bits}]; value: the latest month. values.weeks, optional: the same by week [{week_start, plays, artists, entropy_bits, effective_artists}] while the archive is young.

nostalgia.description: Median release year of what I played, by month: values.months [{month, plays, median_release_year}]; value: the latest month. values.weeks, optional: the same by week [{week_start, plays, median_release_year}].

enduring.description: From Apple Music lifetime counts: values.library {artists, plays, since} and values.artists [{artist, plays, first_added, years, plays_per_year}], top artists by plays per year since first added.

retention_new_artists.description: Share of each month's new artists still played 30 and 90 days later: values.months [{month, new_artists, played_30d, played_90d, share_30d, share_90d}]; value: the latest share_30d. While not enough data yet, values.first_unit says what the first month needs.

artist_survival.description: Do catalog artists (older than 5 years at discovery) stay in rotation longer than new ones, for artists first played since the 2023 Apple Music sync: values.curves [{type: catalog | new, n, median (months, null while over half remain), points: [{months, survival, lower, upper, at_risk}]}] (Kaplan–Meier, months since an artist's first play, the share still in rotation with a 95% band); values.medians {overall, catalog, new} in months (null when not reached); values.hr_a {value, interval} the hazard ratio of new against catalog artists leaving rotation (Cox, unadjusted) and values.hr_b {value, interval} the hazard ratio per five years of gap between an artist's release years and the year I added them; values.logrank {statistic, p}; values.share_catalog (share of discoveries that are catalog, 0 to 1); values.n {catalog, new, total}; values.longest_lived [{artist, type, months, censored}] (censored: still playing); values.cohort, a sentence on who is counted. value: hr_a's value. The how line states the export's earliest recorded play, before which a rotation's end is invisible; the pages quote it.

artist_survival_all.description: The same analysis including the artists already in the library before the 2023 sync, their first play dated from the library: values.curves [{type: catalog | new, n, median (months, null while over half remain), points: [{months, survival, lower, upper, at_risk}]}] (Kaplan–Meier, months since an artist's first play, the share still in rotation with a 95% band); values.medians {overall, catalog, new} in months (null when not reached); values.hr_a {value, interval} the hazard ratio of new against catalog artists leaving rotation (Cox, unadjusted) and values.hr_b {value, interval} the hazard ratio per five years of gap between an artist's release years and the year I added them; values.logrank {statistic, p}; values.share_catalog (share of discoveries that are catalog, 0 to 1); values.n {catalog, new, total}; values.longest_lived [{artist, type, months, censored}] (censored: still playing); values.cohort, a sentence on who is counted. value: hr_a's value. The how line states the export's earliest recorded play, before which a rotation's end is invisible; the pages quote it.

album_listening.description: Albums or songs: values.rows [{album, artist, gini, plays}], each album's Gini coefficient of plays across its tracks (0: every track played alike, 1: one track only); value: the share of albums with Gini under 0.4, the ones played through.

discovery_direction.description: Dig back or keep up: of the tracks added to the library each year, the share released at least 5 years earlier: values.by_year [{year, share_dig_back, n (additions)}]; value and values.share_back, the share overall; values.back and values.keep_up (additions); values.median_release_gap_years; values.sync_additions_left_out.

progress.description: Per main lift, by display name.

relative_strength.description: Per main lift, by display name.

strength_kept.description: Per main lift, by display name.

strength_index.description: Weekly series since the cut started, indexed to 100 at cut start: values.weeks [{week_start, body_weight, strength}], strength being the mean best e1RM across values.lifts, the tracked lifts (by rule: at least 12 sessions in the last 26 weeks; values.untracked names the rest). values.tracked [{name, exercise, sessions, split}]: the tracked set with each lift's sessions in the rule's window, the count it was chosen on; the lifting page shows this count on the lift tiles. values.splits, optional: {chest_back, shoulders_arms, legs}, each {lifts, weeks: [{week_start, strength}]} indexed the same way; values.current {strength, body_weight}; values.lifts_change {lift: {start, latest, change_pct}}. value: the latest strength index. The how line states the selection rule.

retention.description: Per main lift, by display name: change in best e1RM since the cut started (value, lb, with interval); values {start, latest, change_pct}.

volume_lag.description: Correlation of a week's volume with the next week's e1RM change (value: r, with interval); values {lag_weeks, weeks, points [{week_start, volume, next_e1rm_change}]}.

consistency.description: Sessions per week against e1RM change: value r with interval; values.buckets [{sessions_per_week, weeks, mean_e1rm_change}].

best_held_lift.description: The main lift whose best e1RM has changed most for the better since the cut started (strength_index.values.lifts_change).

attribution.description: Title metadata and community ratings are Simkl's; credit them.

s_tier.description: What earns an S: values.by_type [{type, s, titles, share}], values.by_decade [{decade, s, titles, share}] by release decade, and values.over_indexed [{genre, ratio, n}], genres over-represented in S against B (ratio of shares). value: the S share overall.

tier_model.description: Can my tiers be predicted from Simkl metadata: value and values.accuracy_loo (leave-one-out accuracy), values.baseline_accuracy (always guessing the commonest tier), values.features [{name, effect, interval}].

taste_drift.description: Tier by the year I watched: values.years [{year, mean_tier_score, n}] with S = 5 to D = 1; value: the slope per year.

community_gap_by_genre.description: My tier against the community score, by genre: values.genres [{genre, gap, interval, n}], gap in tier-score units, positive where I rate higher.

pace_vs_tier.description: Tier by how fast I watched: values.buckets [{bucket, mean_tier_score, n}] for binge, steady and slow pace.

by_director.description: Mean tier of my finished films by director: values.rows [{name, mean_tier, n, films: [{title, tier}]}], people with at least 3 finished films, best first; mean_tier on the tier scale S = 5 to D = 1. Names and titles are public figures and works.

by_studio.description: Mean tier of my finished anime by studio: values.rows [{name, mean_tier, n, titles: [{title, tier}]}], people with at least 3 finished titles, best first; mean_tier on the tier scale S = 5 to D = 1. Names and titles are public figures and works.

by_lead.description: Mean tier of my finished films by lead actor: values.rows [{name, mean_tier, n, films: [{title, tier}]}], people with at least 3 finished films, best first; mean_tier on the tier scale S = 5 to D = 1. Names and titles are public figures and works.

blockbuster.description: Tier against money and popularity: value is the slope in tier points (S = 5 to D = 1) per unit of log revenue over budget, with interval; values.films_with_money, values.films_with_popularity, values.by_popularity_quartile [{quartile (1 = least popular), mean_tier, n}].

sequels.description: Sequels against their first film: value is the mean first-minus-later tier change (S = 5 to D = 1; positive where the first film rated higher), with interval; values.collections [{collection, first: {title, tier}, later: [{title, tier}], mean_first, mean_later, first_minus_later}].

language.description: English against other languages: values.share_non_english (0 to 1) and values.means {english: {mean_tier, n}, other: {mean_tier, n}}.

critics_vs_audience.description: Where critics and audiences split, which side my tier takes: value is the share siding with critics, with interval; values.films [{title, year, tier, critics, audience, sides_with}]. 'not available from source' without OMDb scores.

crowd_agreement.description: My tier against Simkl's community score: value is the rank correlation; values.points [{title, type, year, tier, tier_score (S = 5 to D = 1), community}] for every tiered title; values.disagreements {above: [three titles I rate furthest above the crowd], below: [three furthest below]}, each {title, type, year, tier, tier_score, community, gap}; values.top_overrated_genre and top_underrated_genre (genre names, where my tiers run furthest above and below the community); values.model_accuracy and values.model_baseline (predicting my tier from the score, leave-one-out, against always guessing the commonest tier).

taste_profile.description: What my tiers respond to: values.rows [{name, effect, interval, clear}] (standardised effects on my tier score, S = 5 to D = 1, of each genre or feature; clear is true when the interval excludes zero), values.model_accuracy and values.baseline (leave-one-out, against always guessing the commonest tier), values.disagreements {above: [...], below: [...]} as in crowd_agreement. value: model_accuracy.

landing.description: Where new places land in my current ranking: value and values.median_percentile, the median percentile (0 to 1, 1 = top) at which the last 20 places I ranked for the first time sit in the current list; values.recent [{place, percentile}], those 20 in order of first ranking, oldest first (no dates); values.months [{month, rankings, median_percentile}] by month of first ranking when there are enough months, else absent.

rerank_drift.description: Score change for places I re-ranked, by time since the first ranking: values.buckets [{since, n, median_change, mean_change}]; value: the mean change overall, with interval.

safe_bet.description: Which cuisines are a safe bet: values.rows [{cuisine, n, median, q1, q3}], one per cuisine with enough places (15), n counting the places in the rows, the middle half of its scores (q1 to q3) and the median; value: the narrowest middle half (q3 − q1) in points. The page sorts narrowest first and names the safest and the widest.

analysis_eating.description: From Beli. Cities may appear; dates never do.

time_budget.description: Hours by weekday across watching, listening and training over the last 8 weeks: values {weekdays, weeks, hours {watching [7], listening [7], training [7]}}.

analysis_stat_quadrant.description: An analysis_stat whose values have a fixed shape. Strength against luck for every team in my leagues: x = all-play win share, y = wins above expected. values.mine are my teams with their week-by-week trail; values.others are the other teams, anonymous. With small_sample true (status ok, n below min_n) the figures are published and tagged as a small sample.

small_sample.description: True when the statistic is published on fewer than min_n units (status ok, n below min_n): the pages draw its chart and numbers as usual and tag the n line "small sample, threshold 10" (min_n). Absent or false otherwise.

value.description: The headline number, when there is one.

values.description: The statistic's figures. Either the full shape (when there is anything to show) or, while not enough data yet, just first_unit: While status is "not enough data yet", values.first_unit (a string) names the first unit of data the statistic needs, as a phrase ("one album with 10 plays in its first week"); the pages show one line, "nothing to show yet: needs <first_unit>", and nothing else: no count of units needed and no date. (available_from is removed.)

label.description: My team's display label, as teams[].name ("Sleeper · 12-team PPR").

league_key.description: Opaque key joining my team to its league's other points ("sleeper-1"); never a league name.

luck.description: Wins above expected: actual wins minus all-play wins.

analysis_stat_draft.description: An analysis_stat whose values have a fixed shape. Every pick of mine against the median for its round (value: the residuals summed). With small_sample true (status ok, n below min_n) the figures are published and tagged as a small sample.

small_sample.description: True when the statistic is published on fewer than min_n units (status ok, n below min_n): the pages draw its chart and numbers as usual and tag the n line "small sample, threshold 10" (min_n). Absent or false otherwise.

value.description: The headline number, when there is one.

values.description: The statistic's figures. Either the full shape (when there is anything to show) or, while not enough data yet, just first_unit: While status is "not enough data yet", values.first_unit (a string) names the first unit of data the statistic needs, as a phrase ("one album with 10 plays in its first week"); the pages show one line, "nothing to show yet: needs <first_unit>", and nothing else: no count of units needed and no date. (available_from is removed.)

round_baseline.description: Median points to date of every player taken in that round, league-wide.

first_unit.description: While status is "not enough data yet", values.first_unit (a string) names the first unit of data the statistic needs, as a phrase ("one album with 10 plays in its first week"); the pages show one line, "nothing to show yet: needs <first_unit>", and nothing else: no count of units needed and no date. (available_from is removed.)

interval.description: 95% interval for value, where one is defined.

n.description: Sample size, in the unit min_n counts (weeks, plays, sessions, places...).
